text:
Ravi Desai: Weird one — after switching our monorepo app to use the new redwood-inference-js@2.3.0 (for typed SDK), several edge routes started throwing "TypeError: model.embed is not a function" in production only. Local and unit tests fine.

Lina Torres: did you change import forms? Types-only refactors can accidentally change resolution if package.json exports/types point somewhere weird.

Ravi Desai: we do `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference-js'` and then `const c = createClient({ key })`. The error implies createClient returned something missing methods.

Marco Ruiz: open the built server chunk (prod build) — you'll probably see a tiny stub where the real implementation got tree-shaken. Bundlers sometimes drop prototype-augmenting modules when package.json has "sideEffects": false and the implementation is split across files.

Ravi Desai: dumped the chunk and grepped: the main class is in `dist/core/index.mjs` but retry/embedding helpers are in `dist/plugins/embed.mjs`. embed.mjs only exports functions and also has a top-level side-effect that patches core prototype. package.json has "sideEffects": false.

Lina Torres: aha — prototype patch via top-level import is a fragile pattern. If embed.mjs is only imported for side-effects (not referenced directly) tree-shakers can remove it. Also FYI there was a types-only change: the `types` field in the SDK package.json pointed at `dist/types/index.d.ts` which re-exports symbols from `./plugins/embed.d.ts` — TypeScript sees the shape but bundlers don't because the runtime import got pruned.

Ravi Desai: so TS shows everything is fine (types re-exported), but runtime is missing. Makes sense why dev didn't catch it until prod bundle.

Marco Ruiz: two options for SDK: 1) avoid prototype patching — compose instead or export named initializer functions; 2) mark the specific plugin files as side-effects in package.json like "sideEffects": ["./dist/plugins/embed.mjs"] so bundlers keep them; 3) add explicit exports in package.json exports map so `import { embed } from 'redwood-inference-js/plugins'` works and users can opt in.

Ravi Desai: app workaround: we added `import 'redwood-inference-js/dist/plugins/embed.mjs'` in our edge entrypoint. That fixed prod immediately but it's a brittle path. Bundle size +6.7KB.

CI Bot: note: Rolling deploy to prod paused while we triage.

Lina Torres: additional wrinkle: some bundlers (esbuild via Vite) will rewrite dynamic imports and even duplicate small CJS wrappers if the package mixes CJS for node and ESM for browsers. That can cause both bloat and mismatched instances (two versions of the same class). Check for duplicated class definitions in the bundle.

Ravi Desai: we found two copies of Client class in different chunks — one used in serverless handler, the other in edge middleware. Instances from one copy lack plugin methods.

Marco Ruiz: SDK team should ensure single canonical export surface in ESM and avoid bundling conditional runtime re-exports. Exports map like: { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" }, "./plugins/embed": { "import": "./dist/plugins/embed.mjs", "types": "./dist/types/plugins/embed.d.ts" } } helps a lot.

Ravi Desai: I'll keep the explicit import for now and pin to 2.2.x for critical routes. Opening internal ticket RW-4510 with repro bundle and diff. https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-4510

DevEx Bot: Created ticket RW-4510: "embed plugin tree-shaken in prod when consuming typed ESM package -> missing runtime methods" — https://redwood.internal/issue/RW-4510 :clipboard:

Lina Torres: long term: add a tiny smoke test in CI that builds a minimal Next+Vite app that imports the SDK and runs a basic call in a simulated edge environment. Catches these exports/sideEffects issues early.

Marco Ruiz: agreed. Also add a doc note in SDK release notes about bundler interactions (sideEffects, exports map) and recommended import patterns for edge vs node.

Ravi Desai: thanks all — saved a postmortem. :tada:
